sample_basis: 20 current-query records per audited source/database where available

lens.current_w01_use: DOI only for identifier-assisted matching; raw Lens payload still contains the other IDs.

openalex.current_w01_use: DOI plus OpenAlex source-local identity; PMID is not mapped into the W01 sidecar.

scopus.current_w01_use: DOI plus Scopus-local IDs; pubmed-id is not mapped.

wos.current_w01_use: PMID is already retained sidecar-only and is available to the test identifier extractor.

pubmed.current_w01_use: DOI, PMID and PMCID are available to the test identifier extractor.

ebsco_medline.current_w01_use: Current EBSCO harvester maps DOI and accession number but drops PMID.

ebsco_psycinfo.current_w01_use: Current EBSCO harvester maps DOI and accession number but drops PMID and UMI.

ebsco_cinahl.current_w01_use: Current EBSCO harvester maps DOI and accession number but drops PMID and database-specific identifier fields.

conclusion: PMID preservation is the highest-value immediate improvement.
EBSCO MEDLINE is the clearest case: all 20 sampled records exposed PMID upstream, but none reached the current W01 identifier representation.
OpenAlex, Lens, Scopus, EBSCO PsycInfo and EBSCO CINAHL also exposed PMIDs that are currently unused or dropped.
Source-local IDs should continue to be retained for provenance/identity but should not be treated as cross-source duplicate evidence unless a second provider exposes the same namespace.
No production W01 files or decisions were modified.
